The teddy bear exists because a president refused to shoot a bear.
In 1902, President Theodore Roosevelt went bear hunting in Mississippi, and after days, he still hadn't found one.
So his guides caught a black bear, tied it to a tree, and told him to take the shot.
Roosevelt refused. He said it wasn't fair.
A cartoonist drew the moment, and it ran in newspapers across the country.
In Brooklyn, a candy shop owner named Morris Michtom saw it.
His wife Rose sewed a little stuffed bear, and he put it in the window, with a sign: Teddy's bear.
It sold out. Then they made thousands more.
So every teddy bear is named after a president who said no.
